page: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine is backed by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Compute capacity consists of 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 16.0 GB, establishing an 8.0 GB per-core allocation ratio. The hardware incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX-512, Intel AMX, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The instance includes a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable single-threaded capacity alongside limitations stemming from the 2-vCPU topology. Single-core evaluations show a stress-ng metric of 1941.89 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1932.0. Single-threaded gzip compression shows higher efficiency at 31.37 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core scaling is bounded by the single physical core, resulting in a stress-ng multi-core score of 1992.08 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2403.0. Uncached large block memory bandwidth records 21.49 GB/sec for reads and 14.29 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, Redis achieves 2.81 million SET operations per second, and static web serving delivers 4.38 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure perspective, the server offers efficient resource density for applications requiring an elevated memory footprint without the expense of higher core counts. The combination of 16 GB of memory and fast local NVMe storage makes the E2ds_v6 suited for memory-bound tasks, including small relational databases, key-value caching layers, data staging micro-services, and lightweight extract-transform-load jobs.
